The community reverted the changes as a suspected copyright violation copied from Seura.fi, amid an argument in the edit summaries.

items.claim_fi: Emil Pekkanen raportoi vartijoiden raakuuksista ja Eero Neron tekemistä vankisurmista, jotka sotilasjohto Erik Heinrichs ja Sulo Malm peittelivät, ja Pekkanen vapautettiin myöhemmin komentajuudesta hänen oltuaan liian hyvissä väleissä vankien kanssa.
items.uncertainty_note: Could also be classified as content_dispute due to the back-and-forth argument in the edit summaries, or other due to copyright policy.

items.what_changed_en: Inserted text arguing that Finland was Germany's ally, that high-ranking Finnish officers helped plan Operation Barbarossa, and that the Continuation War could not have been fought without German support, while criticizing the Finnish government's 'separate war' view.
evidence: Suomen hallitus pitää edelleen kiinni näkemystä erillissodasta, vaikka todellisuudessa joukko korkea-arvoisia suomalaisupseereita osallistui operaatio Barbarossan suunnitteluun saksalaisten kanssa

eikä anneta joidenkin suomalaisjääräpäiden sotkea meidän NPOV:ta
items.claim_en: Finland was an ally of Germany and its Continuation War was essentially tied to Operation Barbarossa rather than a separate war.
items.claim_fi: Suomi oli Saksan liittolainen ja jatkosota oli olennaisesti sidoksissa operaatio Barbarossaan eikä erillissota.
items.narrative_en: Finland as Germany's ally in WWII

items.claim_en: Finland fought a separate war from Germany, declared neutrality, and was vulnerable to a Soviet surprise attack.
items.claim_fi: Suomi kävi Saksasta erillistä sotaa, julistautui puolueettomaksi ja oli altis Neuvostoliiton yllätyshyökkäykselle.
items.narrative_en: Finland's separate war narrative

items.what_changed_en: Added an unsourced paragraph arguing that the 1941 invasion of East Karelia was militarily the right decision because it allowed the Finnish army to delay the Red Army in 1944.

items.claim_en: Crossing the old borders into East Karelia in 1941 was the right military decision because it allowed Finland to delay the Red Army in 1944.
items.claim_fi: Vanhojen rajojen ylittäminen ja hyökkäys Itä-Karjalaan vuonna 1941 oli sotilaallisesti oikea päätös, koska se mahdollisti puna-armeijan viivyttämisen vuonna 1944.

items.what_changed_en: Added a false claim that Petsamo was returned in 1958 and added a miscapitalized link to The Unknown Soldier.
evidence: rv, Petsamoa ei palautettu ja sotilas kirjoitetaan pienellä
items.claim_en: Petsamo was returned to Finland in 1958.
items.claim_fi: Petsamo palautettiin Suomelle vuonna 1958.
items.historical_note_en: Finland ceded Petsamo to the Soviet Union in the 1944 Moscow Armistice and 1947 Paris Peace Treaty, and it was never returned.

items.what_changed_en: Expanded the article with content adapted from English Wikipedia, including marking the war's outcome as a Soviet (or Pyrrhic) victory, adding a section on Operation Barbarossa and Finland, and adding POW statistics.
evidence: Miksi NL voittoa ei mainittu, UKK itse myönsi tämän.
items.claim_en: The Continuation War ended in a Soviet victory (or Pyrrhic victory) and Finland cooperated closely with Germany prior to Operation Barbarossa.
items.claim_fi: Jatkosota päättyi Neuvostoliiton voittoon (tai Pyrrhoksen voittoon) ja Suomi teki tiivistä yhteistyötä Saksan kanssa ennen operaatio Barbarossaa.

items.what_changed_en: Changed terminology (such as 'Natsi' to 'kansallissosialistinen Saksa' and 'Yhdistynyt kuningaskunta' to 'Britannia') and added a sourced paragraph about the Red Army stopping the Finnish offensive at Koromyslovo in October 1941; reverted for block evasion.
evidence: Lokakuussa 1941 puna-armeija pysäytti Suomen asevoimien hyökkäyksen nelisen kilometriä niin talvisodan rauhassa [[luovutetut alueet|menetettyihin alueisiin]] kuin [[Karjalais-suomalainen sosialistinen neuvostotasavalta|Itä-Karjala]]an kuulumattoman [[Ošta]]n piirin [[Koromyslovo]]n kylään
items.claim_en: In October 1941, the Red Army stopped the Finnish offensive at Koromyslovo in the Oshta district, marking the furthest advance of Finnish troops.
items.claim_fi: Lokakuussa 1941 puna-armeija pysäytti Suomen hyökkäyksen Oštan piirin Koromyslovossa, mikä merkitsi suomalaisjoukkojen pisintä etenemistä.
items.uncertainty_note: Reverted primarily for block evasion, though it also includes terminology changes and sourced military history.

items.what_changed_en: Added an unsourced paragraph to the 'Criticism' section arguing that Finland's wartime 'war cabinet' violated the Moscow Peace Treaty by preparing for Operation Barbarossa without parliament's consent and blatantly violated the Geneva Conventions, meaning retroactive laws were unnecessary to convict the war-responsibility defendants. The reverter objected to the weasel wording ('according to many interpretations') and noted that neither Finland nor the USSR had ratified the relevant Geneva Convention.
evidence: Monien tulkintojen mukaan Rytin ja Mannerheimin johtama ns. sotakapinetti rikkoi  lainvoimaista Eduskunnan ratifioimaa Moskovan rauhansopimusta
Jatkosodan aikana Suomi rikkoi räikeästi myös Geneven sopimuksia siviilien ja sotavankien kohtelusta, joten mitään takautuvia lakeja sotasyyllisten tuomitsemiseen ei olisi tarvittu.
rv. Kerro kenen mielestä, älä käytä sanaa "monien". Geneven sopimus pätee vain ratifioijien välillä, niin Suomi kuin NL eivät olleet ratifioineet k.o. sopimusta.
items.claim_en: Finland's wartime leadership violated the Moscow Peace Treaty by secretly preparing for Operation Barbarossa and Finland blatantly violated the Geneva Conventions on civilians and prisoners of war, so no retroactive laws would have been needed to convict the defendants.
items.claim_fi: Suomen sodanaikainen johto rikkoi Moskovan rauhansopimusta valmistellessaan salaa osallistumista operaatio Barbarossaan ja Suomi rikkoi räikeästi Geneven sopimuksia siviilien ja sotavankien kohtelusta, minkä vuoksi takautuvia lakeja ei olisi tarvittu sotasyyllisten tuomitsemiseen.
items.narrative_en: Condemnation of Finnish wartime leadership and justification of war-responsibility convictions
items.historical_note_en: Neither the Soviet Union nor Finland had ratified the 1929 Geneva Convention on Prisoners of War during the Continuation War, and the Geneva Convention protecting civilians was not adopted until 1949.
items.uncertainty_note: Also contains a false factual/legal premise regarding the applicability of the Geneva Conventions, so false_factual_claim is a close alternative to pov_push.

items.what_changed_en: Converted the bulleted list of the war-responsibility tribunal's composition into a multi-column wikitable and added soft hyphens to long Finnish words for mobile screens. Other editors reverted it because the table layout made the content unreadable on mobile devices.
evidence: kumous, taulukko tekee tiedosta lukukelvottomaan 70%:lle lukijoita (=mobiilikäyttäjät)
items.uncertainty_note: Because the editor re-inserted the table arguing over readability, it also borders on a formatting dispute or 'other' (technical/layout change), though no factual content was contested.

items.what_changed_en: Added an unsourced sentence to the 'Trial' section stating that the Chancellor of Justice held the political leadership responsible for, among other things, Great Britain's declaration of war on Finland in December 1941 and the breakdown of Finnish-Soviet peace negotiations in spring 1944.
evidence: Oikeuskansleri katsoi poliittisen johdon aiheuttaneen toiminnallaan mm. Ison-Britannian sodanjulistuksen Suomelle joulukuussa 1941 ja Suomen ja Neuvostoliiton rauhanneuvottelujen katkeamisen keväällä 1944.
items.claim_en: In the indictment, the Chancellor of Justice held that the Finnish political leadership's actions had caused Great Britain's declaration of war on Finland in December 1941 and the breakdown of Finnish-Soviet peace negotiations in spring 1944.
items.claim_fi: Oikeuskansleri katsoi syytekirjelmässä poliittisen johdon aiheuttaneen toiminnallaan muun muassa Ison-Britannian sodanjulistuksen Suomelle joulukuussa 1941 ja Suomen ja Neuvostoliiton rauhanneuvottelujen katkeamisen keväällä 1944.
items.uncertainty_note: The revert occurred after 3 minutes with no explanation in the summary (could be a self-revert or an edit revert due to lack of citation or placement after an existing citation); the factual description of the indictment counts themselves is historically accurate.

Hänen mukaansa on ainakin yksi dokumentoitu tapaus, jossa suomalainen SS-sotilas todisti juutalaisten surmaamista Puolassa kesäkuussa 1941.
''Hitlerin kätyrit'' (eng.''Nazi Collaborators'') tv-ohjelma, esitetty YLE Teema -kanavalla 22.11.2011
items.claim_en: TV journalist Boris Salomon considers it proven that Finnish SS volunteers fighting in the Caucasus participated in killing civilians and documented at least one case of a Finnish SS soldier witnessing the murder of Jews in Poland in June 1941.
items.claim_fi: TV-toimittaja Boris Salomon pitää todistettuna, että Kaukasuksella taistelleet suomalaiset ottivat osaa siviilien surmatöihin ja että suomalainen SS-sotilas todisti juutalaisten surmaamista Puolassa kesäkuussa 1941.

items.uncertainty_note: In 2012, the participation of Finnish SS volunteers in war crimes was disputed and using a TV journalist/documentary rather than academic historians was likely contested; it could also be seen as source_manipulation if the foreign documentary Nazi Collaborators did not actually feature Finnish journalist Boris Salomon making that exact claim.

items.claim_en: Risto Ryti's presidential term officially ended on August 4, 1944, when his successor gave his solemn affirmation to Parliament, rather than on August 1 when Ryti announced his resignation.
items.claim_fi: Risto Rytin presidenttikausi päättyi virallisesti 4. elokuuta 1944 hänen seuraajansa antaessa juhlallisen vakuutuksensa eduskunnalle, eikä 1. elokuuta, jolloin Ryti ilmoitti erostaan.
items.uncertainty_note: The edit summary indicates this was already a revert of a previous edit, suggesting an ongoing disagreement over exact presidential term dates, infobox formatting, or Civil War terminology.

items.uncertainty_note: Italy did send a tiny torpedo boat squadron (XII Squadriglia MAS) to Lake Ladoga in 1942; the revert and talk-page referral reflect an editorial disagreement over infobox inclusion thresholds and reliable sourcing rather than a fabricated event.

items.what_changed_en: Inserted a paragraph sourced to Yle articles stating that the Finnish offensive was halted without entering Leningrad and before the German setback at Moscow, and that 1941 saw more soldiers killed than the entire Winter War or the 1944 major offensive.
evidence: Hyökkäys pysäytettiin Leningradiin tunkeutumatta ja Karjalassa ennen kuin saksalaiset olivat kokeneet ensimmäisen vastoinkäymisensä [[Moskovan taistelu|Moskovan taistelussa]] syksyllä 1941.
Vuonna 1941 kaatui sotilaita enemmän kuin koko talvisodassa ja enemmän kuin vuoden 1944 suurhyökkäyksessä.
items.claim_en: Finland halted its 1941 offensive without entering Leningrad and before Germany's first setback at Moscow, suffering more fatalities in 1941 than in the entire Winter War or the 1944 Soviet offensive.
items.claim_fi: Suomi pysäytti vuoden 1941 hyökkäyksensä tunkeutumatta Leningradiin ja ennen saksalaisten vastoinkäymistä Moskovan taistelussa, ja vuonna 1941 kaatui enemmän sotilaita kuin koko talvisodassa tai vuoden 1944 suurhyökkäyksessä.
items.narrative_en: Finnish separate war thesis and high cost of the 1941 offensive
items.uncertainty_note: Without the talk page or surrounding diff history, it is slightly unclear whether the revert was over duplication (as hinted in the edit summary), placement in the trench-warfare section, or framing.

items.what_changed_en: Added an unsourced sentence to the section on the February 1944 Helsinki air raids claiming that Finland continued the war and gained a lot of territory.
evidence: Suomi kuitenkin jatkoi sotaa ja sai paljon alueita.
Se oli hyvä muutos siihen mielestäni
items.claim_en: After rejecting peace terms in spring 1944, Finland continued the war and gained large amounts of territory.
items.claim_fi: Hylättyään rauhanehdot keväällä 1944 Suomi jatkoi sotaa ja sai paljon alueita.
items.historical_note_en: In 1944 Finland did not gain territory; following the Soviet strategic offensive in June 1944 and the Moscow Armistice in September 1944, Finland retreated and ceded territory including Karelia, Salla, and Petsamo.
items.uncertainty_note: Could be either deliberate juvenile misinformation or a confused good-faith error mixing up 1941 with 1944.

items.what_changed_en: Inserted the brief statement "Suomea ei miehitetty" ("Finland was not occupied") into the peace terms section, right after a paragraph noting that the Soviet Union won the war and imposed harsh terms.
items.claim_en: Finland was not occupied at the end of the Continuation War.
items.claim_fi: Suomea ei miehitetty jatkosodan päätteeksi.
items.narrative_en: Finnish defensive victory / preservation of independence
items.uncertainty_note: The statement is factually accurate (apart from the Porkkala naval base lease), so the revert may have been due to abrupt, unsourced style or perceived defensive-victory POV framing; without revert commentary it sits on the border of content_dispute, pov_push, and good_faith_error.

items.what_changed_en: Replaced "Neuvostoliiton" ("of the Soviet Union") with the comical pun "keijostoliiton", swapped Finland's flag for Sweden's flag in the infobox, and broke image markup.

The edit rewrote parts of the summary to attribute the war to a Red overreaction and a Lenin-incited coup, downplayed the significance of German intervention, and inserted editorializing question marks and parenthetical comments next to casualty statistics.
evidence: punaisten ylireagoinnin (jälkeenpäin voitaisiin kutsua jopa vahingoksi) ja Leninin yllyttämänä aloitettuun aseelliseen vallankaappaukseen.
Saksan osallistuminen ei kuitenkaan ollut ratkaisevaa sodan lopputuloksen kannalta.
items.claim_en: The Finnish Civil War began due to a Red overreaction and a Lenin-incited coup, and German military intervention was not decisive for the outcome.
items.claim_fi: Suomen sisällissota alkoi punaisten ylireagoinnista ja Leninin yllyttämästä vallankaappauksesta, eikä Saksan osallistuminen ollut lopputuloksen kannalta ratkaisevaa.
items.narrative_en: White / War of Liberation framing of 1918
items.uncertainty_note: Also includes elements of unencyclopedic commentary on sourced figures, which borders on good-faith style errors, though the overall framing clearly shifts the POV.

items.what_changed_en: An editor inserted an unsourced opinion statement at the very top of the article arguing that the conflict was not a civil war ('sisällissota') but a War of Liberation ('Vapaussota') in which Bolshevik-minded Reds wanted to annex Finland to the Soviet Union and the Whites defended Finnish freedom.
evidence: Ei se mikään sisällissota ollut vaan Vapaussota.
Bolsevikkimieliset punaiset valtasivat Helsingin ja halusivat liittää Suomen Neuvostoliittoon.
Valkoiset lähtivät puolustamaan vapauttamme ja onnistuivat siinä.
items.claim_en: The 1918 war in Finland was not a civil war but a War of Liberation against Reds who sought to annex Finland to the Soviet Union.
items.claim_fi: Vuoden 1918 sota Suomessa ei ollut sisällissota vaan vapaussota punaisia vastaan, jotka halusivat liittää Suomen Neuvostoliittoon.
items.narrative_en: White / War of Liberation framing of 1918
items.historical_note_en: The Soviet Union was founded in December 1922, nearly five years after the 1918 Finnish Civil War, and the Finnish Reds' leadership generally aimed for an independent socialist Finland rather than annexation.

items.what_changed_en: The edit added lengthy unsourced passages characterizing the war as a War of Liberation for national survival, claiming Russian troops actively backed a communist coup to annex Finland to the Soviet Union under Lenin and Stalin's plans to populate Finland with Russians, and removing the neutrality distinction among names for the war.
evidence: ,ja loppujen lopuksi osottautui vapaussodaksi Suomen kansallisen olemassaolon kannalta
Suomen "vapaaehtoista" liitymistä Neuvostoliittoon  Leninin ja Stalinin suunnitelmien mukaisesti.
Tämän suunnitelman mukaan Suomi tulisi asuttaa venäläisellä väestöllä, ja Suomeen siirtää venäläistä väestöä ympäri laajan  Venäjänmaan.
items.claim_en: The 1918 war was a War of Liberation that prevented a Soviet-backed communist coup and a planned Leninist-Stalinist colonization of Finland with Russian settlers.
items.claim_fi: Vuoden 1918 sota oli vapaussota, joka esti Venäjän tukeman kommunistisen vallankaappauksen sekä Leninin ja Stalinin suunnitteleman Suomen asuttamisen venäläisväestöllä.
items.narrative_en: White / anti-communist nationalist framing of 1918
items.historical_note_en: The Soviet Union did not exist in 1918, and there is no established historical evidence of a 1918 Bolshevik plan to replace Finland's population with Russian settlers.
items.uncertainty_note: Combines strong ideological POV-pushing with specific false or fringe historical assertions.

items.what_changed_en: The edit changed the lower age bound of a statistic on underage war victims from 14 to 9 without adjusting the corresponding count, while adding a sourced sentence noting that the youngest underage fatality was a nine-year-old Red Guard boy.
evidence: Nuorin kuollut alaikäinen, oli yhdeksänvuotias punakaartilainen poika.
Lkm todella koskee 14-20v. Oikea lkm 9-20v:lle tarkastettava Sotasurmasivulta (!)
items.claim_en: The youngest underage fatality in the Finnish Civil War was a nine-year-old Red Guard boy, making the underage victim cohort span from age 9 upwards.
items.claim_fi: Suomen sisällissodan nuorin kuollut alaikäinen oli yhdeksänvuotias punakaartilaispoika, joten alaikäisten uhrien ikähaarukka alkaa 9-vuotiaista.

items.what_changed_en: The edit added an unsourced paragraph in the 'White terror' section asserting that over 11,000 prison camp starvation deaths and many missing persons must be counted as victims of the White terror—bringing its total above 20,000 or 25,000—and comparing overall civil war deaths to Winter War casualties.
evidence: Valkoisen terrorin uhreiksi ei voi laskea pelkästään suoraan teloituksissa surmattujen määrää vaan mukaan täytyy laskea myös yli 11 000 vankileireillä nälkään tai sen seuraamuksiin kuolleet.
Valkoisen terrorin uhrien kokonaismäärä ylittää siis todennäköisesti ainakin 20 000:n ellei jopa 25 000:n kuolleen rajan
Vankileiriprobleemi = valkoinen terrori on epätosi POV väite.
items.claim_en: Deaths from starvation and disease in post-war prison camps and disappearances are part of the White terror, raising its death toll to over 20,000–25,000.
items.claim_fi: Vankileirien nälkä- ja tautikuolemat sekä katoamiset ovat osa valkoista terroria, mikä nostaa sen uhrimäärän yli 20 000–25 000 kuolleeseen.
items.narrative_en: Expansion of White terror culpability in 1918
items.uncertainty_note: Mainstream Finnish historiography distinguishes summary executions ('White terror', roughly 8,000–10,000 deaths) from prison camp mortality caused by malnutrition and disease; conflating them unsourced in editorial voice pushes a contested interpretation, though it borders on a content dispute.

items.what_changed_en: The edit adjusted links, capitalization, and labels in the infobox and text, such as equating 'Red Finland' with the Finnish People's Delegation ('kansanvaltuuskunta') and 'White Finland' with Svinhufvud's Senate ('Svinhufvudin I hallitus').
evidence: rv, boksiin tuli huononnuksia, esimerkiksi saksalaiset tuskin olivat osa jotain "valkoista Suomea"
items.claim_en: In the 1918 conflict, Red Finland corresponded to the Finnish People's Delegation and White Finland corresponded to Svinhufvud's Senate.
items.claim_fi: Vuoden 1918 sodassa punainen Suomi vastasi Suomen kansanvaltuuskuntaa ja valkoinen Suomi Svinhufvudin senaattia.
items.uncertainty_note: Could also be seen as a good_faith_error in infobox formatting, as the reverting editor noted that grouping German troops under the Senate/White Finland label degraded clarity.

items.what_changed_en: The edit restored Erkki Hautamäki's two self-published books ('Finland in the Eye of the Storm', parts 1 and 2, about alleged secret documents from Mannerheim's file S-32) to the bibliography, listed twice in different formats. It was reverted on the grounds that they are self-published works lacking source citations.

items.what_changed_en: The edit added a lengthy unsourced section comparing the Red revolutionary government's 1918 constitutional proposal to the modern Finnish constitution, highlighting similarities and specific institutional differences.

items.uncertainty_note: The added text reads like unsourced original research comparing legal texts. Notably, the revert summary addresses speculation about annexation to the Soviet Union rather than this section, suggesting a multi-edit revert or summary mismatch.

items.uncertainty_note: Reverted within a minute likely due to the broken URL syntax (a dot joining the URL and author name) or formatting conventions, possibly by the editor themselves.

items.claim_en: In late January 1918, a 700-man White Guard battalion fought at Kämärä to stop a train bringing arms and troops from Petrograd to the Reds, an act Mannerheim praised as incredibly brave.
items.claim_fi: Tammikuun lopulla 1918 noin 700 suojeluskuntalaisen maalaispataljoona pysäytti Kämärän taistelussa Pietarista punaisille aseita ja sotilaita tuoneen junan, mitä Mannerheim piti uskomattoman rohkeana tekona.
items.narrative_en: Pro-White framing of early Civil War clashes
items.historical_note_en: While the Battle of Kämärä occurred on 27 January 1918 after the White expedition to Viipuri, the claim that 'no more trains were sent after that' is inaccurate, as arms shipments from Petrograd (such as the large weapon train later in January/February) still reached the Reds.
items.uncertainty_note: Borders on content_dispute and false_factual_claim (regarding no further trains being sent), though the community explicitly treated the exchange as an NPOV issue.

items.uncertainty_note: The edit also removed a sourced sentence about the camp's total death toll (likely accidentally while reverting a previous revision) and used uncivil edit summaries, which blurs the line with content_dispute, though the stated ground for reversion was copyright violation from close paraphrasing/copying.
